To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the higher view is dominant in the perceived image quality at downsampling ratios up to 1/2 (corresponding to 11.6 pixels per visual degree) and that the perceived quality of the lower-resolution stereoscopic view is linearly correlated with its average luma PSNR at downsampling ratios below 1/4 (corresponding 7.6 visual degrees).

(1) in MR stereoscopic videos with downsampling ratio 3/8 or higher, the higher-resolution view is dominant, and (2) in MR stereoscopy with downsampling ratio lower than 3/8 the perceived quality is close to the quality that would be achieved if the lower-resolution view was used without downsampling, and the perceived quality linearlty correlated with the average peak signal-to-noiseratio of the lower-resolution video.

the perceived quality of mixed-resolution stereoscopic videos is close to the perceived quality of the higher-resolution views when the downsampling ratio along both coordinate axes is less than 1/2 (11.4 pixels per degree of view angle), and when it is larger, the perceived quality is close to the quality that can be expected from the lower-resolution view. In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of downsampling ratio on the perceived quality of mixed-resolution stereoscopic images.
finding out what downsampling ratio can be used in MR stereoscopic videos without sacrificing the perceived image quality too much.
the impact of downsampling ratio on the perceived quality of MR stereoscopic video.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the perceived quality of MR stereoscopic video depends on the downsampling ratio and the average luma PSNR of the lower-resolution image.
the downsampling ratio should be kept below 1/2 in order to avoid a significant degradation of the perceived quality.
the downsampling ratio should be no greater than 3/8 in order to achieve good perceived quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a given downsampling ratio, the perceived quality of a MR stereoscopic video can be predicted with a high degree of accuracy from the luma PSNR of the lower-resolution video.
in order to obtain a good perceived image quality, the downsampling ratio in the stereoscopic view that has a lower resolution should be kept below 3/8.

the perceived quality of MR stereoscopic video depends on the downsampling ratio, and that it is possible to predict the perceived quality of an MR stereoscopic video based on the average luma PSNR of the lower-resolution image.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quality of the lower-resolution video should be at least close to the quality that would be perceived if the lower-resolution video was presented in isolation, in order to avoid the quality of the high-resolution video being dominated by the lower-resolution one.
the perceived quality of MR stereoscopic video depends on both the downsampling ratio and the average luma quality of the lower-resolution image.

, for MR stereoscopic video with the downsampling ratios tested, the quality is not necessarily dominated by the higher-resolution view, and the quality is instead determined by the average quality of the lower-resolution views.
